finding.claim: The DELETE handler calls the async authorize() without await. The handler goes on to delete the report before the permission check finishes, so the check never blocks anything. Any request that reaches the route can delete any report, whatever the caller's grants. A failed check also becomes an unhandled promise rejection, which crashes the process on Node 15 and later.
finding.source: Any user, authenticated or not, sending DELETE /reports/:id with an arbitrary id.

trace.note: The report is loaded by the attacker-supplied req.params.id.
authorize() returns a promise that is not awaited. The 403 it throws is never observed by the handler.
db.reports.remove() runs regardless of the outcome.
The handler returns 204, so the client sees success.

finding.guards_checked: The authorize() logic at lines 9-16 would deny correctly if awaited, as the PUT handler does at line 27. No other middleware, error handler or unhandledRejection handler exists. The only app-level middleware (lines 4-7) copies the session user and does no authorization.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws a 403 on a missing grant, but the DELETE handler calls it as a bare statement at line 20 with no await or catch. The only other middleware (lines 4-7) copies the session user and does no authorization. The PUT handler awaits the same check at line 27.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls async authorize() without await, so its rejection is never observed and db.reports.remove runs at server.js:21 and returns 204 at line 22 for any caller who can reach the route, including a low-privilege authenticated user. The claim that unauthenticated callers can also delete depends on a session middleware that is not in this file, but that does not change the verdict.

verdict_facts.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws a 403 on a missing grant, but the DELETE handler's call at line 20 is not awaited. The only middleware (lines 4-7) copies the session user and does no authorization. There is no error handler or unhandledRejection handler.
verdict_facts.reason: At server.js:20 authorize() is called without await, so its rejection is never observed, and db.reports.remove runs at line 21 and 204 is returned at line 22 whatever the grants say. The PUT handler awaits the same call at line 27, which shows the intended behaviour.

finding.claim: The PUT handler passes the whole request body to db.reports.update() without a field allowlist. A user with only the write grant can overwrite any field of the report, such as owner, id or ACL fields, if the data layer accepts them. This is mass assignment.
finding.source: JSON body of PUT /reports/:id from a user holding the 'write' grant.

trace.note: express.json() parses the body into an attacker-controlled object.
The raw req.body is written to the database.

finding.guards_checked: No schema validation or field filtering exists in this file. The db layer is not present, so whether it filters fields is unverified. The impact depends on what the report schema contains.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 is awaited at line 27 and throws a 403 when the 'write' grant is missing. It gates access but does not filter fields. No allowlist or schema validation exists in this file.
verdict.reason: server.js:28 passes raw req.body to db.reports.update() after the awaited 'write' check at line 27, and nothing in this file filters fields. Whether a write-grant user can reach owner or ACL fields depends on the db layer, which is not in the repository (only server.js exists).

verdict_facts.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws a 403 and is awaited at line 27, so it works as a guard, but it only checks the 'write' grant. There is no field allowlist or schema validation in this file.
verdict_facts.reason: server.js:28 passes req.body unfiltered to db.reports.update() after a working write check at line 27, but db is not in this directory. I can't tell whether it accepts or strips fields such as owner or ACL, so the escalation can't be confirmed or refuted.

finding.claim: There is no authentication gate. The code reads req.session.user without checking that a session middleware is installed or that a user is logged in. With no session middleware, req.session is undefined and every request throws a TypeError in the middleware. If a session middleware is added and an anonymous user has no session.user, req.user is undefined. authorize() then throws a TypeError on user.id at line 10. In PUT that failure is an unhandled async rejection. In Express 4 the request hangs and the process may crash. In DELETE (F1) the delete proceeds anyway. This route-level failure is an availability and robustness problem. Combined with F1 it lets unauthenticated users delete reports.
finding.source: An unauthenticated request with no session user.
finding.sink: Protected operations at lines 21 and 28, plus an unhandled rejection that can crash the process.

trace.note: req.user is set from req.session.user with no check that it exists.
user.id is dereferenced with no null check.
db.reports.get() can return null for an unknown id. The next line then reads report.id and throws, again as an unhandled rejection.

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware, no try/catch around the async handlers, no error-handling middleware, and no express-async-errors wrapper. Whether crashes occur depends on the Node version and the Express version, which cannot be checked here because there is no package.json.

verdict.guard_found: none: no auth middleware, no try/catch, no error middleware, and no async-errors wrapper. The only control is authorize() at server.js:9-16, and DELETE calls it without await at line 20.
verdict.reason: server.js:5 reads req.session.user unchecked and server.js:10 dereferences user.id, so an anonymous request makes authorize() reject. The DELETE handler calls authorize() without await at server.js:20, so db.reports.remove runs at line 21 anyway, and in PUT (server.js:27) the same rejection is unhandled. The trace is slightly off: the trace note for line 19 says the next line reads report.id, but that read is at line 21, not line 20. The file also has no session middleware or db definition, so reachability depends on code outside it.

verdict_facts.guard_found: none. The only control is authorize() at server.js:9-16, which throws on failure. DELETE calls it without await at server.js:20, so the rejection is dropped and server.js:21 still runs. PUT awaits it at server.js:27, but there is no try/catch, error middleware or login check.
verdict_facts.reason: No authentication gate exists (server.js:5 sets req.user without a check), and the un-awaited authorize() at server.js:20 lets an anonymous request reach db.reports.remove at server.js:21. In PUT the failure is an unhandled rejection at server.js:27 with no catch. The crash and hang behaviour depends on the Express version, which is not available here, but the unauthenticated delete does not depend on it.
